newsitem.title: CROATIA: Belgian UN soldier killed by young Serb - UN.
newsitem.headline: Belgian UN soldier killed by young Serb - UN.

text.p: The man who killed a Belgian corporal and injured two other U.N. personnel in the Serb-held town of Vukovar in eastern Croatia on Friday was identified by U.N. sources as a young Serb with a criminal record.
The suspect was arrested after a shooting incident on the main road near the headquarters of the U.N. Transitional Administration of Eastern Slavonia (UNTAES) in Vukovar.
"The U.N. car was driving by when this crazy guy pulled an automatic weapon and started shooting at us," said a U.N. source, speaking on condition of anonymity.
The source has identified the arrested suspect as "a young Serb male with a criminal background".
The Belgian Defence Ministry named the soldier as Corporal Olivier Gossye, and said he had died in the line of duty.

Defence Minister Jean-Paul Poncelet said in a statement an inquiry had been opened to determine whether the death of Gossye was the result of an isolated criminal act or an attempt at destabilisation.
Gossye was the first U.N. casualty in Eastern Slavonia, except for fatal traffic accidents, since the U.N. troops were deployed in the region in spring 1996.
A Jordanian soldier and an UNTAES civilian officer from Ivory Coast were wounded in the incident. They were taken to Vukovar hospital, and the officer was later discharged.

U.N. Secretary General Kofi Annan, now in Switzerland, condemned "this act in the strongest possible terms and issued his condolences to the relatives of the Belgian soldier", U.N. spokesman Juan-Carlos Brandt said in New York.
The United States condemned the incident but said it appeared to be the act of a single individual, not a broad threat to peace.
"The United States strongly condemns the attacks today on the United Nations soldiers by a Serbian gunman," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said.
He said the attack "appears to be the act of a single individual" who is now in police custody and under United Nations supervision.
Vukovar is the biggest town in the Serb-held region of Eastern Slavonia which is due to return to Croatian government rule by mid-June.

A series of incidents have increased tension there as the local Serb population becomes increasingly nervous with the approach of the deadline for the "peaceful reintegration" of the region into Croatia.
The Croatian government on Friday blamed the killing on local Serb leaders trying to slow down the reintegration.
"The incident is undoubtedly a result of the delaying strategy promoted by some local Serb leaders," Hina news agency quoted Croatian ambassador to the U.N. Mario Nobilo as saying.
"They and their actions have encouraged the extremist elements who committed this abhorring crime," Nobilo said.

But Goran Hadzic, one of the leaders of the Serb community, disagreed. "All the known facts of this grave incident show that it had no political background or goal, nor was directed against the members of the UNTAES forces," Hina quoted him as saying.
"It was simply a result of an unfortunate course of events, caused, to a great extent, by the psychosis and developments in the past few days," Hadzic said.
A Belgian military plane is expected to fly Gossye's coffin back to Belgium on Saturday, U.N. spokesman Philip Arnold said.
